quotes.text: Parents deserve both clarity and control over how their children interact with AI chatbots, which are becoming more integrated into their education and everyday lives. Our bipartisan bill provides commonsense guardrails that prioritize kids’ safety, limit manipulative design, and help ensure that parents—not algorithms—hold the reins.

Is it possible that TikTok had enough data—could get enough data on me that you could use artificial intelligence and your algorithms and machine learning to write an algorithm that could persuade me to change how I view a policy issue? Does that possibility exist?

We’ve talked a lot about, this Chinese model that’s been developed for artificial intelligence and, supposedly, it’s been done cheaper and better than the United States. Color me skeptical. [...] And then second, can we acknowledge this is TikTok on steroids, right? If we’re worried about the influence of the CCP on America with TikTok, this is on steroids.

Congress must help encourage AI innovation, but not without transparency and accountability. The CLEAR Act strikes the right balance by protecting creators’ intellectual property while providing clear expectations for companies. By shedding light on how generative AI models are trained, our bipartisan legislation will help build public trust for emerging technologies and foster the best of American creativity.
As AI-generated content becomes more refined and realistic, people deserve to know whether what they’re seeing is created by a human or generated by artificial intelligence.

Parents deserve confidence that AI tools are not exposing their children to harmful content, fostering unhealthy emotional dependence, or exploiting their personal information. We need clear standards for transparency, accountability, and child safety so families can navigate the opportunities and risks of emerging technologies with confidence.

Americans deserve representation in Congress that is not only well-informed on cutting-edge AI development, but also has the wherewithal to cross the aisle and overcome political pressures to address the concerns these technologies pose.

That is why we are calling for immediate public hearings to bring lawmakers, model makers, and other stakeholders into the same room and work through solutions that maintain America’s competitive edge in development while ensuring that these technologies serve human interests and remain fully under human control. In the meantime, Congress must ensure necessary safeguards are in place.

AI has enormous potential, and it’s critical that the United States continue to lead the world in its development. But innovation and accountability have to go hand in hand. [...] This bill provides that protection without creating another federal regulator or standing in the way of responsible innovation.
And it’s this lack of wisdom that makes AI, without human control, so dangerous.

A machine doesn’t need evil intentions to cause enormous harm. It only needs the ability to do something dangerous without the wisdom to understand why it shouldn’t. Imagine extraordinary analytical intelligence applied to biological weapons research, nuclear weapons, cyberattacks, or any number of other areas where the consequences of getting something wrong could be catastrophic.

I believe these risks deserve to be discussed with the same seriousness that surrounded nuclear proliferation in the 1950s and 1960s, which is why I’ve called for public hearings and joined my colleagues in introducing targeted legislation.
Will AI dramatically change employment? Almost certainly. Will it eliminate entire categories of jobs? Very possibly. Will it create new jobs we haven’t even imagined? I suspect so.

We are deeply concerned by reports that the recently departed CEO of the nation’s top semiconductor company, NVIDIA, was caught in a honeypot scheme with a Chinese spy and executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm known to help Chinese companies circumvent export controls. Our concerns about insufficient export controls on these technologies are magnified by numerous rogue artificial intelligence incidents, including autonomous hacking incidents, unauthorized agent access to the internet, and attacks on real-world targets. Whistleblowers from the nation’s leading AI companies have warned that technology is accelerating without sufficient guardrails, further compounding our concerns.

Collectively, these incidents show the urgent need for the Trump administration to act and protect the safety and security of Americans. Responsible U.S. domestic AI policy must promote our competitive edge in artificial intelligence through reasonable innovation and regulation. It should not enable our strategic adversaries to embrace risky behaviors with these technologies or to acquire them through nefarious means. China’s frontier artificial intelligence capabilities are rapidly approaching those of the United States, with some experts estimating China’s frontier to be just six to nine months behind the United States…To maintain its competitive edge while promoting responsible domestic AI policy, the United States must ensure Chinese AI labs cannot easily procure the compute required to develop, test, and train advanced artificial intelligence models.

We urge you to condition licenses for the export of advanced AI chips on an agreement that recipients will not provide Chinese companies with remote access unless granted a separate and additional license to do so. These policies should not be geographically limited in scope. If they are, China will simply rent access to chips elsewhere, creating a whack-a-mole scenario.

During your confirmation hearing, you called for stronger export controls, saying, ‘If they are going to compete with us, let them compete, but stop using our tools to compete with us.’ Today, the stakes are clear, and our adversaries are not playing by the rules. We must close these loopholes if the United States is to maintain its competitive edge in artificial intelligence.
